completion_decisions: Implement all eight paper accuracy sizes and the 95-turbine 12-state optimization problem.
Use FLOWFarm as an equation and data lineage oracle only because its public sparsity source postdates the target paper.
Preserve the paper size sequence and public-layout ring counts while explicitly reporting the conflict with the stated 5.1D minimum spacing.
Use pure C++ fixed-width forward dual blocks, conflict-graph coloring and the target adaptive threshold and pattern-update lifecycle.
Complete the omitted optimizer as deterministic projected gradient ascent with Armijo backtracking and the omitted spacing as a disclosed 2D FLOWFarm-documentation completion.
Run five declared thresholds for all eight accuracy sizes and ten common starts with both dense and sparse gradients.
Use all available Waffle cores for target runs and one worker only for the bounded H6 scaling reference.

paper.authors: Benjamin T. Varela and Andrew Ning
paper.title: Sparsity for Gradient-based Optimization of Wind Farm Layouts

paper_source_conflicts: The 5.1kD radius and at-least-5.1D ring-spacing statements conflict with the exact size sequence and public 38-turbine fixture, which imply floor(6.4k) ring counts and approximately 5D chord spacing.
FLOWFarm's substantial unstable-sparsity implementation begins in February 2024, after the 2023 target paper, and cannot be represented as target source.
The paper conclusion mentions three optimized problems while the explicit optimization experiment describes ten starts of one 95-turbine problem; the reproduction follows the explicit experiment.
